text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah visits National Guards camp, urges increased performance.
- Kuwait's private sector foreign workers amount to 620,000 people. Kuwait has a population of two million people with 720,000 nationals.
- Kuwait Airways Corp (KAC) increases economy class air fares for children to 67 percent of full fare from 50 percent.
- Dust storms expected to continue until the end of August.
- Kuwait's Social Reform Society starts Jordan charity branch. The Society is widely believed to be Kuwait's arm of the Moslem Brotherhood movement.

- Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah says looking forward to return to Kuwait. Sheikh Saad has been abroad since March when he left Kuwait for medical attention in Britain after an emergency colon surgery.

- Health Ministry to watch, weigh drugs ban. Kuwait has instructed state-run hospitals to stop giving non-Kuwaiti patients 81 types of medicine in a cost-cutting move angering some doctors and foreign residents. Kuwait has traditionally provided medicine at state hospitals free of charge.
